finalText:
**Almost always, it is the parent.** When a parent re-renders, React re-renders every child under it. It does not compare props first. Same props change nothing by default.

`React.memo` turns that comparison on. But it compares by reference, not by looking inside the value.

That is where people get stuck. Any object, array, or function written inline is a brand new value on every render. So `style={{margin: 4}}` and `onClick={() => save(id)}` never match the previous one, even though they look identical. Wrap them in `useMemo` or `useCallback` and `memo` starts doing its job.

Two other causes worth a glance. If the child reads a context, it re-renders whenever that value changes, memo or not. And in development, `StrictMode` renders everything twice on purpose.

One comfort: a re-render is not a DOM change. React compares the output and usually touches nothing.
